metric: verbatim quote rate and entity-name presence, as reported by build_site.py --check-grounding

not_applicable.precision: There is no negative class. A quote is in the document or it is not; nothing is predicted that gold could contradict.
not_applicable.citations without a quote: Outside the check by construction. Counted in citation_reach rather than scored.

notes: An audit of the corpus that exists, not a held-out evaluation: there is no split and nothing is predicted about unseen data.
The check is build_site.py --check-grounding, shelled out and parsed. It is not reimplemented here, so these numbers describe the shipped tool.

Citation reach is 97.6% (6516 of 6678 citations carry a quote). `quote` is optional in the schema -- 'only for pivotal events, not every one' -- so a citation with only a page number is outside this check entirely.

--check-grounding concatenates every source file belonging to a subject before searching, so a quote from one document is checked against that subject's whole corpus. That is the shipped behaviour and is reused as-is.

Fabrication and misquotation are reported apart, because collapsing them is misleading in both directions. 213 quote(s) share under half their 5-word shingles with the source and are the real finding; 550 are mostly present but not verbatim, which over PDF-extracted text is usually a curly quotation mark, a ligature or a line-break hyphen rather than an invented sentence. Read quote_fabrication_rate, not quote_verbatim_rate, as the hallucination number.

19 subject(s) covering 41 document(s) are excluded from every rate above: source text is staged as data/<slug>.txt, keyed by subject rather than document, so a subject's second document overwrote the first one's text. Both still point at that one path, so the losing document's quotes are checked against a paper they did not come from. That is a staging bug, not an extraction failure, and its quotes are unverifiable rather than wrong: berthollet, bordet, c_barnard, cartwright, denning, frost.

Diagnostic, not a second verdict: of the 213 quotes the checker calls NOT IN SOURCE, 69 match once whitespace is ignored and 1 more once case is too -- the model emitting a quote with its spacing destroyed, not an invented sentence. 139 are absent in any form, which is 2.58% of all 5394 checked quotes and is the number to read as fabrication.
subjects with unverified quotes: meyer (43/57), wren (25/25), graunt (24/36), g_borelli (23/24), aleskovskii (23/57)
